Epoxides are three-membered cyclic ethers that are highly reactive due to ring strain. They are electrophilic and can undergo ring-opening reactions.

Dithiocarbamates are compounds containing the functional group R2NC(S)S-, which are nucleophilic.

When nucleophilic dithiocarbamates react with electrophilic epoxides, they can potentially cause:
- Violent polymerization (option I): Epoxides are known to undergo ring-opening polymerization when mixed with nucleophiles
- Heat generation (option D): The ring-opening reaction is exothermic
- Potentially toxic gas generation (option H): Sulfur compounds can sometimes release toxic gases

Without specific experimental data, I believe the most likely serious hazard is violent polymerization, as epoxides are known for this behavior when mixed with nucleophilic compounds.
